newsitem.title: USA: Jury deadlocked over damages in Food Lion/ABC case.
newsitem.headline: Jury deadlocked over damages in Food Lion/ABC case.

text.p: A federal jury said Friday it was deadlocked and unable to agree on whether Walt Disney Corp.'s ABC Television unit should pay punitive damages to Food Lion Inc.
"We can go no further," the jury said in a note to U.S. District Judge Carlton Tilley. The note was read aloud in the courtroom at the end of the panel's fourth day of deliberations.

But Tilley immediately told the jury of six men and six women that they must try again to reach a verdict. He ordered the panel to return to the courthouse in Greensboro on Tuesday, following a federal holiday on Monday.

The foreman of the jury told the judge, "There hasn't been a situation where all 12 agree on any aspect of the entire verdict sheet." Jurors began deliberations on Tuesday after the judge gave them a 12-page verdict worksheet to fill out in determining if ABC and four of its producers should pay punitive damages for a 1992 "PrimeTime Live" report about Food Lion.

"Take the weekend off. Do something that's fun," Tilley told the jurors in an effort to encourage the panel to eventually reach a decision. When the judge asked if any of the jurors could reach a final decision if deliberations were to resume on Tuesday, seven of the jurors raised their hands to indicate "yes."

Bill Jeffers, a lawyer for ABC, asked the court out of the jury's presence whether the panel should be forced to reach a consensus, suggesting he was opposed to the measure, but lawyers for Food Lion said they supported the decision, and Tilley declined to change his mind.
